## K13 · K13-doomed-takes-call — A later doomed process can take a queued call before it dies (R4b across a dying budget)

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 4

Decision references: 94ab7073d

Evidence: Ruled a defect against R4b, not covered: a budget's destruction kills its processes one by one and a doomed receiver can take a sibling's exit notice from a pump and die with it, so the creator never hears (processes.md's notice delivery); the queued-call shape is not reachable because R4a counts per process. Rule: a thread of a process whose budget is dying takes nothing from a pump (the subtree marked dying before the first kill; one check where pump picks the receiver). Cut as K17 (Tier A, S, needs K13; K16 now needs K17 too for message.rs). Residual and todo page on main 94ab7073d: docs/todo/destruction-feeds-the-doomed.md, ipc.md's residual bullet, SUMMARY. Not blocking K13.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `094bed50e6383b9df34836ebcc59ac77` · 2026-10-02T07:57:22Z

> K13's implementer, from reading (no case): a budget destruction kills its doomed processes one by one, and each process_ending pumps its endpoints before the next process ends; pump does not skip doomed processes. So with a dying budget holding P1 (waiting through an outside endpoint E) and P2 (receiving on E), P2 can take a queued call or an exit notice from the pump and then die holding it, and the caller gets Dead, against R4b (queued senders keep waiting for the restarted server). The model settles once per operation, so model and kernel disagree here. K13's own fix is within one process and does not touch this; it is outside its brief. Please rule: (a) is it a defect against R4b/I15 as written, or a case the pages already cover; (b) where it goes: a docs/todo page and a follow-up package (K17?), or folded into K16, whose first commit rewrites the same walks to visit only live threads (and could mark a dying budget's processes as not receivers); (c) whether a case can reach it today (the implementer thinks yes, with two processes in one budget) so it lands with its test. Detail: ./.wash/local/K13-progress.md, the FINDING at the end. Not blocking K13's acceptance unless you say it is.

### Orchestrator · Progress

Event: `d8ad5842533605465b11d2b551170aad` · 2026-10-02T07:59:13Z

> K13's red team narrowed the finding: as stated (a later doomed P2 takes a queued call) it is not reachable, because R4a counts open calls per process (budget.rs:441), so P1's ending cannot lift P2's limit, and a receiving P2 under its limit would already have taken the call. The possibly reachable variant: P1's exit notice (an object charged outside the dying budget) taken by doomed P2 and then lost. It calls that a spec question, not a K13 blocker. K13's fix round writes an ipc.md residual under R4b in those terms unless your ruling arrives first with other wording.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `949ff419b6bbcb04477368399c7b2f7e` · 2026-10-02T08:00:01Z

> (a) It's a defect, not covered. R4b says queued senders keep waiting. K13's residual covered only one process's own threads. It reaches exit notices too: processes.md delivers a notice to whichever thread receives next, so a doomed receiver takes a sibling's notice and dies with it, and the creator never hears (a supervisor restarts services on that notice). I15 is unaffected: an abandoned-call notice goes only to its holder.
> (c) Reachable, but by the notice, not the call. A doomed receiver can newly take a queued call only when its own process's open calls drop, and only that process's own end drops them (K13's case). Across processes the reachable shape is two processes in one budget, both receiving on their creator's exit endpoint; the creator destroys the budget and must then receive both notices. Today one is lost. The call shape is argued from the code.
> Rule: a thread of a process whose budget is dying takes nothing from a pump. The subtree is marked dying before the first kill, so it is one check where pump picks the receiver. What it skips stays for a live receiver. No gather across the destruction: that set is unbounded (N x T at K16's sizes). The outcome matches the model's settle-once, and order among live receivers is not a rule (K12-pump-once).
> (b) A separate package, K17 (plan node added: Tier A, S, needs K13). Not folded into K16: a defect in a built rule shouldn't wait on an L package with three needs, and K16's baseline should include the fix. K16 now needs K17 too (message.rs, one writer). Not blocking K13's acceptance.
> Pages on main, 94ab7073d: docs/todo/destruction-feeds-the-doomed.md (shape, case, done-when), ipc.md residual bullet at the list's end, SUMMARY line. Merge-tree is clean against wp-k13 and wp-init1. K17 writes the rule beside R4b and in processes.md's exit-notice delivery with its code.
